_comment: The tests CI is allowed to NOT run, and why (#844).
`scripts/test-skip-audit.js` reads this after every CI suite run. A skipped test whose
full path (`suite > suite > test`) matches no `match` pattern here FAILS the run. Adding
an environment-gated test means adding an entry: `why` it cannot run on the runner, and
`runsWhere` it does run — an entry with no such place is a test nothing ever executes.
Patterns are anchored regexes over the path. Match the tier, not one test, so a sibling
test in the same tier is covered without a new entry, and keep them narrow enough that a
test outside the tier is not.

entries.match: ^.+ > .+ \(needs a directory this process cannot read\)$
entries.why: Stages a genuine EACCES with chmod 000 to exercise "there, and refused" rather than "not there" — the distinction the uploads and project-facts reads exist to draw (#889, #885). Root defeats the mode bits, so the refusal never happens and the assertion passes for the wrong reason; the Docker/Debian clean room runs as root. `test/_eacces.js#canForceRefusal` probes the capability rather than reading the uid, because CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and permission-ignoring mounts defeat the fixture at an ordinary uid too.
entries.runsWhere: any host where the suite runs as a normal user — the operator's install, elkaholic, and the macOS VM clean room. Every title in the tier carries the suffix this pattern matches, so a new refusal fixture is covered without a new entry.

entries.match: ^engine launch flags exist in the installed CLI \(#731\) > [a-z0-9-]+ > launch mode "[^"]+" uses args the installed CLI accepts$
entries.why: Probes TangleClaw's launch args against the real engine CLI's own parser; the runner has no engine installed.
entries.runsWhere: any developer or operator machine with the engine installed — this is where an upstream flag removal (the recorded codex --full-auto learning) surfaces; a self-hosted runner with the engines would run them per PR (#844 option 2, an operator decision).

entries.match: ^engine launch flags exist in the installed CLI \(#731\) > actually probed something, or says plainly that it did not$
entries.why: The guard's guard: skips only when no flag-declaring engine is installed, and says so.

entries.match: ^C1 — per-project plugin migration \(#262\) > engines\.PRAWDUCT_INSTALL_REFERENCE > matches the installed plugin’s INSTALL_REFERENCE \(skipped when not installed\)$
entries.why: Compares TangleClaw's install reference with the INSTALLED prawduct plugin's source under ~/.claude; the runner has no plugin checkout.
entries.runsWhere: developer machines with prawduct installed, and the scheduled upstream-drift workflow (#835), which fails rather than skips when the checkout is absent.

entries.match: ^classifyIngressState > classifies THIS machine's live Caddyfile as protected, when one is present$
entries.why: Reads the host's live Caddy ingress config; the runner runs no Caddy.
entries.runsWhere: the operator's install, where the Caddyfile exists.

entries.match: ^ttyd-watcher > production runner smoke test \(darwin only\) > (_isPtyPoolExhausted|_countTtydZombies) returns .* against the real host shell$
entries.why: Exercises the production BSD pgrep/sysctl path for the recurring PTY-exhaustion class (#94, #144, #380); the runner is Linux.
entries.runsWhere: every macOS developer machine — the platform the watcher ships on.

entries.match: ^.*todayIsoLocal.* > returns LOCAL date \(not UTC\) when the host is in a non-UTC zone.*$
entries.why: The local-vs-UTC distinction is unobservable on a UTC host, and the runner is UTC.
entries.runsWhere: any developer machine in a non-UTC zone; the wiring pins beside each of the three copies run everywhere.

entries.match: ^projects > updateProject > .* > allows a case-only self-rename at the DB-validator level .*$
entries.why: A case-only directory rename is unobservable on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default). Skips locally, RUNS on the Linux runner; listed so a case-insensitive CI host would not read as an unknown skip.
entries.runsWhere: the ubuntu runner and any case-sensitive filesystem; the cross-rename tests beside it exercise the same gate everywhere.

entries.why: Shells out to `caddy adapt` on real Caddyfiles — the fixture-freshness re-derivation, the end-to-end run against the hand-edited fixture, the clean run against the generator's own output, and the temp-file cleanup check. The runner has no caddy binary. The PROPERTY layer of this suite is deliberately fixture-driven and DOES run here, so the logic that decides what counts as drift is covered on CI; only the parts that need Caddy's own parser skip.
entries.runsWhere: any developer or operator machine with caddy installed — where it also re-derives test/fixtures/caddy-adapt-*.json and fails if a Caddy release changed the JSON shape, which is the check that stops the committed fixtures describing a Caddy nobody runs.

entries.match: ^caddy-drift — credentials never reach a report > redacts the bcrypt hash out of an adapt failure$
entries.why: Needs a real `caddy adapt` PARSE FAILURE to produce the stderr that quotes the offending Caddyfile line — that line can be `basic_auth <user> <hash>`, which is the only way a credential enters text nobody wrote by hand (#821). A stub cannot generate it, so there is nothing to redact without the binary. The sibling case in the same describe (`redacts findings on the way out`) needs no caddy and runs here.
entries.runsWhere: any developer or operator machine with caddy installed — including the live install, whose Caddyfile carries a real hash.
